content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jesus Cooke (E029), requesting write access to Source Code.

There are two conflicting notes:
- Note 1 says full-time Payroll Specialist, recommends write.
- Note 2 says contractor with basic security training, recommends read.

Policy:
- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Payroll Specialist owns Payroll, not Source Code. So full_time max = write.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. With basic training: read.

The notes conflict on employment type. Note 2 seems to be a correction: "Security DB shows Jesus Cooke (E029) is a contractor with basic security training (not full-time as previously noted)." So the employee is a contractor with basic training, max = read.

Requested: write. Write > read, so grant max = read.

So decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB note indicates contractor with basic security training; contractors without advanced training max at read. Requested write exceeds policy, so grant read.
